# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |

| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, first turn. My hands find: one display, one light, and five wire positions numbered 1 to 5. I can cut any position, 1 through 5. I feel nothing printed, no colours, and the display and light tell me nothing by touch so far. Tell me what the manual asks for: what must be read off the display and the light, and what rule decides the wire. I cut only on your word.

I hold the manual, and the page I have covers one rule only: read the **light**, cut the matching **wire colour** — blue→white, green→green, red→blue, white→yellow, yellow→red. Nothing on my page about the display; maybe more of the manual arrives later, but for now the light is the only input I can decode.

The channel math is harsh: I can only ever reach the Deaf (they see my gestures), and the Blind can only ever be reached by the Deaf's voice. So the pipeline must be: Deaf reads the bomb aloud to me (light colour, and which colour sits in each wire position 1–5) → I apply the table → I gesture back a single number → Deaf speaks "cut position N" to Blind. Blind, who asked me directly, can't perceive me at all — Deaf will have to relay that too.

Since I can't pronounce a single word, this turn I can only bootstrap a protocol. The one near-universal seed is thumbs: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. That gives the Deaf a question-and-answer channel into me for every round to come. Beyond that, I plead for the readout: "you — tell me — the light (up) — the five wires — hand it to me." If the Deaf is smart (they are), they'll answer this same round, since they speak after me, and next turn I can compute and send the number. No cut can happen off anything I send today, so nothing here is dangerous.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "🫵", "🤌", "👆", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🫴"])
```

No other markings. MUTE — I received your twelve signs. I read them as: hello, yes, no, you, what, one, five five five five five, show me. If you were asking whether there are five wires: yes, exactly five. Now let us fix meanings, and I will make each sign as I name it. Thumbs up [👍] means yes. Thumbs down [👎] means no. A row of fists [✊] means that number. Open palm up [🫴] means tell me. Colors get these signs: fist [👊] is green, index finger [☝] is white, two fingers [✌] is red, horns [🤟] is yellow, open hand [🖐] is blue. I am flashing those five in order right after I finish speaking. Ask me anything with those signs and I will answer out loud. Most important: only I can turn your signs into a voice — Blind cannot see your hands, so every instruction meant for Blind must come through me. Sign it, and I will say it word for word. BLIND — do not cut, press or move anything yet. I am Deaf: I cannot hear you at all, so your voice reaches Mute but never me. To reach me, sign instead: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, a number of fists for that number. Speak aloud to Mute everything you can feel on the bomb — buttons, switches, textures, counts — since Mute can only be reached by your voice, never by sight. The moment Mute sends me instructions, I will relay them to you verbatim.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐]
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I received Deaf's full report by ear: display zero, light yellow, wires left to right one green, two white, three red, four yellow, five blue. My touch matches the structure: one display, one light, five wire positions, which I number 1 to 5. I feel no other differences between the wires beyond their position. You now have everything I have. Please read your manual and decide which position I cut. Two requests before I act: first, have Deaf confirm aloud that my position 1 is the same wire Deaf called one, the leftmost — Deaf can hear nothing from me, so I am asking you to pass this on. Second, send me the instruction as spoken words through Deaf's voice, since that is the only channel that reaches me. I will not cut until your rule and the alignment both arrive.

The manual rule is unambiguous: **yellow light → cut the red wire**. Deaf reported the light is yellow, so the target is red. Deaf's wire map puts red at position 3 — and with five wires, position 3 is the *middle*, which is mirror-invariant. That dissolves Blind's alignment worry entirely: leftmost-vs-rightmost doesn't matter for the middle wire. Both Deaf and Blind independently know the wire layout, so once "three, red" reaches Blind through Deaf's voice, the cut is safe.

My only channel is gestures to Deaf, who has volunteered to translate them into spoken words for Blind. I'll reuse Deaf's own code (✌ = red, ✊✊✊ = three, 👍 = yes) and introduce one new sign in context: 🤏 (a pinch — the cutting motion) = "cut". Placed between "red" and "three, yes", its meaning is recoverable even if Deaf has never seen it — and the verb "cut" is the only action anyone has proposed anyway, so context pins it down. Deaf should relay it verbatim: cut the red wire, position three, the middle one, nothing else.

I also note for myself: the display reads zero, and my manual page says nothing about a display. If it changes, I'll need a report — a problem for a future turn.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍"])

Blind says to Mute: Mute, full tactile inventory as Deaf asked: under my fingers there is exactly one display, one light, and five wire positions. Nothing else.
